findings.explanation: Carried forward from the previous ai-findings.json review. The resource now sets service_account = var.service_account and the example wires in a dedicated google_service_account.appengine — resolved by commit 785525a ("fix: add explicit service account, handler login, fix KMS rotation and logs bucket").
findings.title: App Engine standard version has no service_account — defaults to the App Engine default SA which carries project Editor in older projects

findings.explanation: Carried forward from the previous ai-findings.json review. The handlers block now sets login = lookup(var.app, "login", "LOGIN_REQUIRED"), defaulting to authenticated access — resolved by commit 785525a.
findings.title: URL handler had no login requirement and no IAP — application was publicly accessible without authentication

findings.explanation: Carried forward from the previous ai-findings.json review. rotation_period is now "7776000s" (90 days), matching the standard used across the author's other modules — resolved by commit 785525a. The resource has since moved to example/examplea/kms.tf but the fix still holds.
findings.title: KMS key rotation_period = 100000s (~28 hours) in example — far below the standard 90-day minimum, will cause excessive re-encryption

findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket.code and google_storage_bucket.logs both set encryption.default_kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name, and google_storage_bucket_object.code_package sets kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name — all three resolve to google_kms_crypto_key.appengine_key via the example's module call. Setting these attributes only tells GCS which key to use; it does not grant access. GCP requires the GCS service agent to hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key before the bucket or object can actually be created/written. This is now fixed: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.gcs_cmek.tf grants that role to the GCS service agent resolved via the data "google_storage_project_service_account" "gcs_account" data source, and all three CMEK-using resources carry depends_on = [google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.gcs_cmek].
findings.title: GCS buckets and objects reference a CMEK, but the GCS service agent is never granted decrypt/encrypt access to that key

findings.explanation: google_app_engine_firewall_rule.allow (priority 1000) permits var.allowed_source_range. examplea.auto.tfvars:11 now sets this to "203.0.113.0/24" (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3), a public (non-RFC1918) placeholder documented in-line as standing in for the caller's real public CIDR — fixed. It's no longer structurally impossible for the allow rule to match a genuine internet client falling through to google_app_engine_firewall_rule.default_deny's catch-all.
findings.title: App Engine firewall allow-rule uses a private RFC1918 source range, so with the default-deny catch-all every real internet client is blocked

findings.explanation: example/examplea/examplea.auto.tfvars:2 now sets app.runtime = "python312", a currently supported App Engine standard runtime — fixed. script_path was also changed from "main.app" to "auto" (required for gen2/Python 3 runtimes using entrypoint-based deployment) and runtime_api_version = "1" (a Python 2-era attribute) was removed, since both were legacy settings carried over from the python37 config that would otherwise have broken deployment on python312. A deterministic check for this now exists as the built-in HLD_GCP_556 (policies/gcp/app-engine/standard-deprecated-runtime.yaml in JamesWoolfenden/holden, committed to main and installed on PATH), though it still lands as UNKNOWN on this repo's own root module for the same reason HLD_GCP_189 does — runtime is var.app["runtime"], a module-call variable indirection holden can't resolve across the module boundary from example/examplea's now-literal tfvars value.
findings.title: Example pins App Engine standard runtime to "python37", a runtime on Google's App Engine deprecation schedule

suggested_policies.implementation_note: Imported into this project's .holden/policies/ as local-gcp-001-app-engine-deprecated-runtime.yaml and confirmed loading without error. It lands as UNKNOWN rather than FAIL on this repo's own example, for the same structural reason HOLDEN_AI_006 was filed: runtime here is var.app["runtime"], a module-call variable indirection holden can't resolve across the module boundary from example/examplea's literal tfvars value — the same blind spot HLD_GCP_189 already hits on service_account. The policy still fires as a deterministic FAIL on any config that sets runtime to a literal deprecated value directly on the resource. HOLDEN_AI_006 itself stays open: adopting the policy codifies the check going forward, it doesn't fix the still-present python37 value in examplea.auto.tfvars.
suggested_policies.rationale: google_app_engine_standard_app_version has no deterministic check on its `runtime` attribute: coverage_by_type for this type in this scan lists only HLD_GCP_189 (service account). This repo's own example pins runtime = "python37" (see HOLDEN_AI_006), one of several App Engine standard runtimes Google has deprecated on a published schedule. A deployment pinned to a deprecated runtime stops receiving security patches once support ends and risks a forced, unplanned migration — the same risk pattern holden already codifies for other compute services via deprecated-runtime checks, just missing for App Engine standard.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: App Engine standard version must not use a deprecated runtime
principle: patch-management
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Google deprecates App Engine standard runtimes on a published schedule.
  Once a runtime's support window ends it no longer receives security
  patches, and Google eventually blocks new deployments and may force a
  migration. Pinning `runtime` to an already-deprecated value means the app
  is running, or will soon run, on an unpatched language runtime.
message: |
  runtime is set to an App Engine standard runtime identifier that Google has
  deprecated.
remediation: |
  Move to a currently supported runtime, e.g.:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_app_engine_standard_app_version" "main" {
    runtime = "python312"
  }
  ```
  Check https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/runtimes for the
  current support table before picking a replacement.
resources:
  google_app_engine_standard_app_version:
    path: runtime
    not_one_of:
      - python27
      - python34
      - python35
      - python36
      - python37
      - nodejs6
      - nodejs8
      - nodejs10
      - php55
      - go111
      - go112
      - ruby25
